P.text: Input x is negative or zero to the Solidity Ln.ln function; the reference Python ln128_prec includes assert digits > 0 requiring positive inputs.
P.evidence_quote: The reference Python code snippet (`ln128_prec`) in the research paper reflects this mathematical domain by including an `assert digits > 0`, explicitly requiring positive inputs.

I.text: ln(x) is mathematically defined only for positive real numbers; non-positive inputs should revert or return an error/NaN.
I.evidence_quote: The natural logarithm `ln(x)` is mathematically defined only for **positive real numbers**. For negative numbers or zero, it is undefined in the real number domain

V.text: Ln.ln lacks input validation: negative inputs are processed using absolute value (ln(-10.0) returns ~2.302585 same as ln(+10.0)), and zero returns a finite negative number (~-18781) instead of -infinity.
V.evidence_quote: `Ln.ln(-10.0)` returns the exact same result as `Ln.ln(+10.0)`, approximately `2.302585`
